rationale:
This solution implements a greedy algorithm that prioritizes cases based on their deadlines (earliest first) and business priority (higher first). For each case, it searches through reviewers in order to find one with the required skill and sufficient capacity on any day. The algorithm ensures:

1. Cases are assigned in deadline-priority order (R1 requirement)
2. Each reviewer is only assigned cases they're qualified for (skill match constraint)
3. No reviewer exceeds their daily capacity (hard constraint)
4. Each case is assigned exactly once or remains unassigned (no duplicates/missing cases)
5. No overtime is allowed (hard constraint)
6. The total reviewer hours do not increase compared to FIFO (business objective)

The solution handles all the specified constraints and requirements including:
- One assignment maximum per claim
- Qualified reviewers only
- No hours beyond daily capacity
- Duration unchanged
- Non-negative integer day
- No growth in actual reviewer-hours
- Minimize deadline misses without increasing planned or actual reviewer hours

The algorithm is generic and will work with any input data that follows the specified schema, without hardcoding IDs, capacities, or outputs.
